sweep_summary: pola1249 Polari (not in catalog). One bibliography title hit, Devís Herraiz 2011 (Glottolog 678746, doi:10.4995/rlyla.2011.897): downloaded open-access PDF and landing page, and. It is a false positive on the Italian word 'polari' ('polar' yes/no questions): a ToBI intonation study of Italian L2 by Madrid Spanish speakers, with no mention of the Polari cant and nothing on word stress in it. Relevance: other language; priority none. No first-hand Polari word-stress statement exists in the works with stress in the title; the prior check's already records that Polari has no phonological description in Glottolog and that the only stress data are IPA stress marks in Baker's Fantabulosa dictionary (Open Library search-inside fragments, verified held by the project). list of works to obtain for acquisition remains Baker 2002 'Polari: The Lost Language of Gay Men' ch. 3 (Routledge, doi:10.4324/9780203167045-6) and Hancock 1984 'Shelta and Polari' (CUP), both lending-only/paywalled; expected to describe Polari as English-embedded lexis, so any stress statement would likely defer to English.

sources.note: Nothing on stress or phonology beyond one IPA form (zhoosh /ʒʊʃ/). Bibliography lists Baker 2002 (both books), Baker 2019 Fabulosa!, Elmes & Rosen 2002.
